preamble: Proto-Tai *ɓ appears as w in southern Shan, where standard Shan and Tai Nüa have m and Thai and Lao keep b (Proto-Tai *ɓaɰᴬ 'leaf' > Shan မႂ်, southern ဝႂ် wǎue). The evidence is limited to dialect forms listed in Wiktionary, and it is unclear whether w comes straight from the implosive or through an intermediate *m or *ʔw, so the change is given with low certainty.

examples.note: Standard Shan မႂ်, Thai ใบ.
Beside မိၼ်, Thai บิน.

sources: Pittayaporn, P. (2009). The Phonology of Proto-Tai. PhD dissertation, Cornell University. https://hdl.handle.net/1813/13855
